title: Grated pear pancakes with yoghurt and honey

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Flour, eggs, milk, butter, pears, Greek yoghurt and honey are all ordinary kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, whisk, grater and frying pan, and spooning pancakes into a pan is beginner technique.

works.reason: 200g self-raising flour, two eggs, 250ml milk and two grated pears make a sensible thick batter for about a dozen pancakes, enough for four, and 2 minutes a side over a medium heat will cook them through.

honest_times.reason: Whisking, grating, slicing and frying in batches add up to roughly the 25 minutes printed, which suits a quick breakfast.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Pears are in the batter and on top, so they are the point of the dish, and warm spiced pancakes suit a December morning.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit-filled pancakes made with eggs and served with Greek yoghurt make a proper breakfast a family would happily eat again.
